title: Perf suite: codify workload matrix + pin prompt sets + reproducible runner scripts (hardware profiles validation)
creator: Claire Dubois
description:
## Context
We need a stable, repeatable benchmark suite to validate the hardware tuning profile pack (H100/B200/L40S) and to power perf-canary gates. Today the perf suite is a mix of ad-hoc scripts + partially documented workload assumptions, which makes it hard to compare results across:
- GPU SKUs / instance types
- regions/pools
- runtime builds
- profile pack versions

This ticket codifies the workload matrix (what we run), pins datasets/prompt sets (what we run it on), and ships a reproducible harness runner (how we run it) so that “baseline vs tuned” comparisons are meaningful and can be automated.

## Goals
1) Workload matrix is explicit, versioned, and checked into the benchmark repo (no more “spreadsheet as source of truth”).
2) Prompt sets / datasets are pinned with immutable identifiers + manifest (hashes), with a clear update process.
3) Runner is reproducible: given (runtime build, profile pack, matrix version, prompt set version) we can re-run and get comparable results.
4) Output artifact format is standardized for dashboards + perf-canary gates.

## Non-goals
- Creating new kernels or new runtime knobs.
- Customer-specific benchmark variants (those can be layered later).
- Perfect determinism at the token level. The goal is stable perf measurement with bounded variance and clear provenance.

## Deliverables
### A) Workload matrix codification
Add `matrix.yaml` (or equivalent) as the canonical matrix definition:
- Model families: representative set used for profile validation
  - “chat-7b”, “chat-13b”, “instruct-70b” (exact model IDs referenced via model catalog pin in the runner config)
- Modes:
  - streaming chat
  - non-streaming completion
  - embeddings (optional phase 2; keep out of initial perf gating)
- Sequence buckets (prompt_len / gen_len):
  - short: (128 / 128)
  - medium: (512 / 256)
  - long: (2048 / 256)
  - xlong: (8192 / 256)  [guarded: only where supported; used to stress KV-cache + fragmentation]
- Concurrency levels:
  - 1, 8, 32 (and 64 for H100/B200 pools only)
- SLO focus tags:
  - latency-sensitive (tail focus)
  - throughput-sensitive (tokens/sec focus)

Matrix entries should have:
- required GPU sku(s) (H100/B200/L40S)
- required runtime features (e.g., streaming, tool-calling on/off)
- warmup settings
- run length (min wall time and/or min tokens)
- metrics to export and expected variance bounds

### B) Pinned prompt sets + manifests
Create versioned prompt sets with a manifest file:
- `promptset_id` (e.g., `hwprof-chat-v1`)
- file list + sha256
- generation parameters (temp/top_p/max_tokens) as part of the manifest
- a clear “update rubric” for Applied ML review (to keep distributions realistic without causing constant churn)

Storage:
- keep a checked-in manifest; payload stored in a versioned internal bucket
- runner downloads by `promptset_id` + version + sha256 verification

### C) Reproducible runner scripts
Implement a single entrypoint that:
- resolves the matrix
- resolves model pins (model IDs and runtime compatibility)
- downloads and verifies prompt sets
- captures environment provenance:
  - GPU sku string, driver, CUDA version
  - runtime git SHA / build id
  - profile pack version and override source
  - container image digest (if applicable)
- runs with fixed seed for request ordering and jitter controls
- outputs a standardized artifact:
  - json summary for each matrix cell
  - merged “suite summary” artifact
  - raw timeseries (optional) for debugging

### D) Standard metrics and artifact schema
At minimum per matrix cell:
- tokens/sec (prefill and decode where possible)
- p50/p95/p99 latency (TTFT, time per output token, end-to-end)
- error rate (timeouts, OOM, retries)
- GPU memory (peak, steady, fragmentation proxy if available)
- queue depth / backpressure events

Also export “profile selection provenance” fields so we can segment dashboards:
- selected profile name
- profile version
- override source (default / per-pool / per-deployment / manual)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Matrix definition lives in repo and is referenced by CI/perf-canary.
- [ ] Prompt sets are pinned by ID+version with sha256 verification; runner fails fast on mismatch.
- [ ] Two engineers can reproduce the same run within defined variance bounds (documented) on the same SKU/pool.
- [ ] Results artifact is consumable by perf-canary (Aisha/Allison) without manual massaging.
- [ ] Documentation: README covering how to add a new matrix entry, how to bump prompt set versions, and how to interpret artifacts.

## Implementation plan (proposed)
1) Draft matrix.yaml based on the Confluence workload matrix doc (Claire)
2) Create initial prompt set manifests:
   - `hwprof-streaming-chat-v1`
   - `hwprof-nonstream-completions-v1`
   - `hwprof-longcontext-stress-v1` (guarded)
3) Implement runner + artifact writer
4) Add “provenance capture” hooks (read GPU/driver/CUDA; read runtime build id; capture profile pack selection)
5) Wire to CI and a nightly job (separate infra ticket if needed)

## Open questions
- Do we treat embeddings as part of the initial gating matrix or phase 2? (current proposal: phase 2)
- How do we handle MIG and multi-GPU nodes in runner scheduling? (should be a tag/constraint in the matrix)
- What variance bounds are acceptable for p95/p99 on L40S (given runner flakiness + memory pressure)?

## Notes
This ticket is a prerequisite for making “expected behavior” docs credible; without pinned workloads, we can’t confidently attribute regressions to profile changes vs workload drift.
comments: 2025-11-05 (Claire Dubois): Created ticket. We need matrix-as-code + pinned prompt sets before we can start claiming baseline vs tuned deltas are real. Also aligns with SRE request for concrete rollback thresholds based on repeatable metrics.

2025-11-08 (Rina Kobayashi): Drafted initial matrix.yaml structure locally. Using tags per cell: `latency_sensitive` / `throughput_sensitive` / `long_context_stress`. Need Applied ML sign-off on prompt distribution and tool-calling patterns (even if tool-calling is disabled initially).

2025-11-12 (Jonas Weber): Please ensure prompt sets include a realistic mix of short system prompts + medium user turns + some “burst” long prompts. Also flag entries that use structured output / JSON mode since that changes token patterns and can affect decode throughput.

2025-11-15 (Rina Kobayashi): Added manifest format proposal (promptset_id, version, sha256, generation params). Plan: store payloads in internal bucket, commit manifest + small sample to repo for review. Runner verifies sha256 before running.

2025-11-18 (Sahana Iyer): CI note: to keep runtime PR signal clean we should split runs into (1) smoke matrix for pre-merge and (2) full nightly matrix. Recommend runner supports `--matrix-filter` and deterministic request ordering. Also we need to cap runtime per job to avoid queue backups.

2025-11-20 (Aisha Bello): For perf-canary integration we need a stable artifact schema. Please include both TTFT and end-to-end p95, and a clear error_rate definition (timeouts vs 5xx vs OOM). Also include selected profile + override source so we can segment dashboards by profile.

2025-11-22 (Rina Kobayashi): Implemented runner prototype and artifact JSON. Captures GPU sku string variants and normalizes to `h100`, `l40s`, `b200` where possible. Still need to add driver/CUDA capture and container digest capture. Will follow up with Infra if we need additional metadata in runners.

2025-11-27 (Claire Dubois): Reviewed matrix contents. We should explicitly guard xlong (8192/256) to avoid false negatives on L40S. Add `requires_min_vram_gb` field and skip with a clear reason in artifacts (don’t mark as failure).

2025-12-02 (Rina Kobayashi): Opened PR benchmark-lab/pr-1842 with matrix runner + artifact schema + manifest verification. Added `--fail-on-skip=false` default for guarded cases, and exports skip reasons for dashboards. Requesting review from Aisha (artifact needs) and Sofia (workload assumptions).

2025-12-06 (Sofia Ivanova): Workload matrix looks good, but make sure streaming tests include a steady-state window. We’ve seen TTFT improvements hide decode tail regressions. Please add a per-cell `min_output_tokens` and report time-per-output-token p95.

2025-12-10 (Rina Kobayashi): Addressed review feedback: added steady-state decode metrics, added environment provenance capture (driver/CUDA), and documented variance bounds guidance (initial: tokens/sec +/- 3% on H100, +/- 5% on L40S; p95 latency bounds per mode TBD). Marking ticket In Review pending PR merge + CI wiring follow-up.
